raw_data_sources:
- source_description: >-
    Raw audio recordings of the acoustic tasks, captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice application on a
    tablet with a headset microphone.
  source_type: primary collection
  raw_data_format: WAV audio
  access_details: >-
    Not included in the PhysioNet release. Retained but not publicly accessible; disseminated
    through controlled access only, via Synapse at https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/,
    with requests directed to the access committee at DACO@b2ai-voice.org.
- source_description: >-
    Questionnaire, demographic, confounder and diagnostic data captured through the collection
    application and held in REDCap.
  source_type: primary collection
  raw_data_format: REDCap export
  access_details: >-
    Exported and converted with the project's open source b2aiprep library into the released
    phenotype tables.

preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Raw audio was standardized by converting to monaural and resampling to 16 kHz with a Butterworth
    anti-aliasing filter applied.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Spectrograms were computed from the standardized audio using the short-time Fast Fourier
    Transform with a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a 400-point FFT, then downsampled by a
    factor of two in the time domain. Mel spectrograms use the same parameters with 60 Mel bins, and
    60 Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients were extracted from the spectrograms.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Articulatory features were generated with the Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package, giving
    kinematic traces of vocal tract articulators and source features together with measures of
    loudness, periodicity and pitch, all gathered at 50 Hz.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Phonetic posteriorgrams, a time-varying categorical distribution over acoustic units of speech
    at 100 Hz across 40 phoneme categories, were generated with the ppgs package.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Acoustic features were extracted with openSMILE, and phonetic and prosodic features — measures
    of fundamental frequency, formants and voice quality — were computed with Parselmouth and Praat.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Transcriptions were generated using OpenAI's Whisper Large model.

cleaning_strategies:
- cleaning_details: >-
    An audit protocol was applied: generate missingness tables; check distributions and outliers;
    check categorical responses against the schema; run quality control metrics for audio tasks;
    and for waveforms check the amount of silence and the duration, and for speech check the
    produced speech relative to the intended passage. All processing was performed with the
    b2aiprep and SenseLab toolkits.
- cleaning_details: >-
    Audio quality control metrics derived from the raw recordings are released alongside the
    features as audio_quality_metrics.tsv, one row per audio recording.

labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: >-
    Gold standard diagnostic labels were taken from clinical assessment. At each site a local
    clinician provided the diagnosis; for the psychiatric disorders cohort the label was determined
    from the participant's electronic health record or an active prescription.
  annotations_per_item: 1
  annotator_demographics:
  - >-
    Typically the clinician at the site of data collection, or a clinician external to it where a
    prior diagnostic assessment was used.
  data_annotation_protocol: Per Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes.
  data_annotation_platform: >-
    The collection application and REDCap, with clinical validation recorded in the diagnosis
    instruments.
  notes: >-
    Human-level performance on the applications the dataset is meant to address is reported to vary
    widely.

machine_annotation_tools:
- tools:
  - OpenAI Whisper Large
  - openSMILE
  - Praat
  - parselmouth
  - torchaudio
  - Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
  - ppgs
  - b2aiprep
  - SenseLab
  tool_descriptions: >-
    Whisper Large generated the transcriptions. openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth and torchaudio
    generated the static acoustic, phonetic and prosodic features and the time-varying spectral
    representations. sparc generated articulatory estimates and source measures; ppgs generated
    phonetic posteriorgrams. b2aiprep organized and preprocessed the dataset and merged the source
    data into the phenotype files; SenseLab processed the audio files for research tasks.
  tool_accuracy:
  - >-
    Certain aspects of the data, for example transcription, were generated using off-the-shelf
    models that have not been audited for correctness.

missing_data_documentation:
- missing_data_patterns: >-
    Phenotype data files contain a row for a participant only if at least one column is not missing,
    and each participant answered a common set of questions plus additional questions relevant to
    their primary diagnostic category. Feature files omit recordings for which a given feature could
    not be generated, whether because of length or other issues.
  missing_data_causes: >-
    Optional questionnaire items, data collection irregularities, cohort-specific branching of the
    instruments, and removal of representations derived from sensitive records and audio checks.
  handling_strategy: >-
    The dataset was audited internally for missingness and consistency by the data release team, and
    a missingness table is included with the dataset.

anomalies:
- anomaly_details: >-
    Different sites have different collection configurations, and the collection protocol changed
    over the course of the study.
- anomaly_details: >-
    Noise artifacts, variations in diagnostic practices, inaccurate questionnaire responses and
    underreporting are possible confounding factors in the collected data.
- anomaly_details: >-
    Recordings were made with a head-mounted headset and microphone that could be at slightly
    different distances between sessions, and the clinical diagnosis, depending on the disorder, was
    performed by one clinician or based on an electronic health record or prescription.

known_biases:
- bias_type: selection_bias
  bias_description: >-
    Participants were recruited at a small number of high volume expert clinics; groups that have
    less trust in the medical system or in AI, or who are less proximal to the collection sites,
    would have been less likely to be recruited.
  mitigation_strategy: >-
    The project states an intention to shift toward remote collection and to design recruitment so
    that more variables are controlled.
- bias_type: representation_bias
  bias_description: >-
    The dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors, and the
    public releases do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories.
  mitigation_strategy: >-
    Users should consider the multivariate distribution when assessing utility for different
    questions.
- bias_type: measurement_bias
  bias_description: >-
    Participants were screened for different disorders based on site, so participants with different
    labels also had their data collected on different devices, confounding label with recording
    apparatus and site.
  affected_subsets:
  - >-
    All disease cohorts, since cohorts were recruited at different sites with distinct iPad devices.

known_limitations:
- limitation_type: representativeness_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The dataset is a non-probability sample of a larger, ongoing collection and is not
    representative, having been collected at a limited number of geographic locations.
  scope_impact: >-
    Limits the generalization of models derived from the dataset to other populations and settings.
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Communication with participants and the collection instruments were in English, and eligibility
    required the ability to read and speak English; Spanish versions of the protocol are described
    as under development.
  recommended_mitigation: >-
    Treat findings as specific to English-speaking participants until non-English collection is
    released.
- limitation_type: scope_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The public release contains data considered low risk — derivations such as spectrograms and
    other features — and not the original voice recordings, which are available only through a
    separate controlled access process.
- limitation_type: temporal_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Changes in diagnostic criteria or practices over the collection period could be a source of
    distribution shift.
- limitation_type: integration_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The multimodal data described in the collection protocol — laryngoscopy and other imaging,
    genomic sequencing, spirometry and other measures extracted from electronic health records — is
    not part of this release, which distributes audio-derived features, per-recording metadata and
    phenotype tables only.
  source_caveats: >-
    The project documentation states explicitly of the preceding release that "no external data is
    released in this v3.0.0 release"; the version 3.1.0 data description likewise lists only
    features, metadata and phenotype content.

content_warnings:
- content_warnings_present: true
  warnings:
  - >-
      Free speech tasks: where transcriptions of free speech are present, offensive, insulting or
      threatening content cannot be completely avoided, since research participants are responsible
      for their choice of language.
  - >-
      Questionnaire content covering mental health, traumatic life experiences and other distressing
      subject matter is collected in the mood and psychiatric cohort instruments.
  source_caveats: >-
    The warning about free speech transcriptions is the project documentation's healthsheet answer.
    In the PhysioNet releases, transcripts of free speech audio were removed from version 1.1 and
    spectrograms and similar features were excluded where the audio contained free speech, so the
    exposure in version 3.1.0 is narrower than the documentation's answer implies.

sensitive_elements:
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    The dataset includes race and ethnicity information and sexual orientation information.
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    The dataset includes socioeconomic and health information, including clinical diagnoses across
    voice, neurological, psychiatric and respiratory conditions.
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    Voice itself is a biometric characteristic capable of identifying the speaker, which is why all
    raw voice data was removed from the registered access release and is disseminated only under
    controlled access.

confidential_elements:
- confidential_elements_present: false
  confidentiality_details: >-
    The project documentation records that the dataset does not contain data considered confidential
    in the sense of legal privilege, doctor-patient confidentiality, or the content of individuals'
    non-public communications.

is_deidentified:
  identifiable_elements_present: false
  method: >-
    HIPAA Safe Harbor, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of non-identifying but
    highly sensitive fields, and by withholding of all raw audio.
  identifiers_removed: >-
    HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers, including names, geographic locators, date information at a
    resolution finer than years, phone and fax numbers, email addresses, IP addresses, Social
    Security numbers, medical record numbers, health plan beneficiary numbers, device identifiers,
    license numbers, account numbers, vehicle identifiers, website URLs, full face photos, biometric
    identifiers and any unique identifiers; state and province, with country of data collection
    retained; select geographic or demographic identifiers and some information about household
    composition or cultural identity; and non-identifying but highly sensitive elements such as
    household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences.
  deidentification_details: >-
    All raw voice data was removed because it has the potential to cause individual re-identification
    or to be used for illicit or unauthorized purposes, and only extracted features are released.
    Raw audio transcripts were reviewed and any recordings containing potentially identifying
    information or external voices were removed from the release; spectrograms and similar features
    were excluded where the audio contained free speech, while static and other features that do not
    encode the sensitive information were retained. Sensitive fields flagged in the REDCap data
    dictionary were removed. K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved.

participant_privacy:
- anonymization_method: >-
    Removal of direct identifiers, removal of indirect identifiers where their combination with
    other public data created a significant risk of re-identification, and release of features
    extracted from the audio in place of the audio itself.
  privacy_techniques: >-
    Withholding of all raw voice recordings from the registered access release; Review and removal
    of recordings containing potentially identifying information or external voices; Removal of
    transcripts and derived representations of free speech; Removal of fields encoded as sensitive
    in the REDCap data dictionary.
  reidentification_risk: >-
    Voice is unique to the speaker and cannot be fully de-identified, so raw audio is disseminated
    only through controlled access to authorized researchers; K-anonymization with k of two or more
    is not achieved for the released tables. Recipients of the raw data are contractually barred
    from using it, alone or with any other information, to attempt to contact the individuals who
    are its subjects.
  data_linkage: >-
    Records are linked across sessions and across feature and phenotype files by a study
    participant identifier; consenting participants also permitted investigators to access medical
    information through electronic health record platforms in order to perform gold standard
    validation of diagnoses and symptoms.

data_protection_impacts:
- impact_details: >-
    The project documentation answers directly that no analysis of the potential impact of the
    dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted.

human_subject_research:
  involves_human_subjects: true
  irb_approval:
  - >-
    Data collection and sharing was approved by the University of South Florida Institutional Review
    Board. The multi-site protocol was submitted to and approved by the USF Single IRB, with subsite
    IRBs reviewing through the Single IRB process; the protocol provides that Canadian institutions
    apply separately to their own research ethics boards.
  ethics_review_board: University of South Florida Institutional Review Board
  regulatory_compliance:
  - >-
    HIPAA de-identification rules were applied to the released dataset. The data transferred under
    the Data Transfer and Use Agreement is covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality, which must
    be asserted against compulsory legal demands such as court orders and subpoenas for identifying
    information or characteristics of a research participant. The study was not conducted for a drug
    product or a medical device, and no data monitoring committee was appointed.
  special_populations:
  - >-
    Enrollment for the cohort released here is limited to adults, with a minimum age of 18 years and
    a maximum age of 120 years; pediatric participants were enrolled only through the pediatric sites
    and are released as a separate dataset. The protocol nonetheless lists "Obtaining Signed Assent
    for Children or Adults Unable to Consent" among its consent options, and the adult cohorts
    include participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, and
    mood and psychiatric diagnoses. The protocol notes that questions asked of participants in
    certain disease cohorts, such as mood disorders, depression and anxiety, can cause discomfort and
    trigger negative emotions.

ethical_reviews:
- reviewing_organization: University of South Florida Institutional Review Board
  review_details: >-
    Data collection and sharing for the released dataset was approved by the University of South
    Florida Institutional Review Board; the clinical study was submitted and approved by the USF
    Single IRB and by subsite IRBs through the Single IRB process. The IRB protocol records that
    Canadian participating institutions do not fall under the Single IRB process and apply
    separately to their own research ethics boards, with copies of those approvals submitted to the
    USF IRB.

informed_consent:
- consent_obtained: true
  consent_type: >-
    Prospective written informed consent, obtained on paper, electronically through REDCap survey
    forms within the application, or by video recording of the participant reading a consent
    statement aloud; assent was obtained where applicable for participants unable to consent.
  consent_documentation: >-
    Paper consent documents are uploaded and saved electronically in REDCap, and all paper and
    electronic versions of consent are stored for a minimum of five years after completion of the
    study.
  consent_scope: >-
    Research data that does not contain direct identifiers is shared with external researchers for
    future research through a secure database: data posing a low risk of individual re-identification
    is shared in registered access with the general public, and data that would pose a heightened
    risk if shared in full open access is shared through a controlled access mechanism with
    authorized researchers. The consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes, to a
    specific geographic location, to a specific type of research, to genetic research, or to research
    that does not involve the development of methods or algorithms.
  withdrawal_mechanism: >-
    Participants are informed that they may withdraw from the study at any point.

collection_consents:
- consent_details: >-
    All participants were duly informed and agreed to the collection and use of their data via
    prospective informed consent, through an IRB-approved consent process conducted by research
    assistants in the clinic or remotely.
- consent_details: >-
    In clinic, potential participants were given time to consider and ask questions, were asked to
    explain what they had understood to the research assistant to confirm understanding, and were
    informed that participation is voluntary and does not affect their medical care in any way.

consent_revocations:
- revocation_details: >-
    Consenting participants are informed that they may withdraw from the study at any point. If a
    participant withdraws during or before the voice data collection, their data is not included in
    the database. Participants are informed that research data, including voice recordings, cannot
    be removed from the database once the voice data collection process is completed. Participants
    who withdraw may optionally complete a satisfaction survey about their reasons for withdrawal;
    no protected health information is collected in that survey.

collection_notifications:
- notification_details: >-
    Individuals were notified about the data collection: participants went through an IRB-approved
    consent process in which the data being collected, the methods used to secure it and the uses to
    which it would be put were explained.

at_risk_populations:
  special_protections:
  - >-
    Enrollment for the cohort released here is limited to adults: the minimum age is 18 years and the
    maximum age is 120 years, and pediatric participants were enrolled only through the pediatric
    sites, which are released as a separate dataset.
  - >-
    The IRB protocol lists "Obtaining Signed Assent for Children or Adults Unable to Consent" among
    the consent options available under the study.
  - >-
    The protocol records that questions asked of participants in certain disease cohorts, such as
    mood disorders, depression and anxiety, can lead to possible discomfort and could trigger
    negative emotions for the participants.
  assent_procedures: >-
    Where assent applies, the protocol provides that it be documented on a dedicated form; for young
    children who cannot reasonably be asked to assent due to limitations in understanding by age and
    development — typically children under seven years of age — assent is not sought.
  source_caveats: >-
    The sources do not state whether the adult cohorts released here include participants enrolled
    through assent rather than personal consent, and no source characterizes this release's
    population as including or excluding at-risk groups, so no such determination is recorded. The
    adult cohorts do include participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and
    other dementias, and with mood and psychiatric diagnoses.

participant_compensation:
- compensation_provided: true
  compensation_type: Electronic gift cards
  compensation_amount: >-
    40 US dollars for a data collection session taking less than 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for a
    session taking over 90 minutes, for no more than three sessions and maximum compensation of 120
    US dollars.
  compensation_rationale: >-
    Compensation for the participant's time; compensation was provided to the adult population only.

license_and_use_terms:
  license_terms: >-
    The files are released under the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, and access requires
    signature of the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement. From version 3.0.0 the PhysioNet
    access policy is that only credentialed users who sign the data use agreement can access the
    files; no additional training is required. Raw audio is governed separately, requiring a Data
    Access Request Form, a Data Use Agreement, review by the Data Access Compliance Office and a
    Data Use and Transfer Agreement signed by an authorized official at the recipient institution.
    Duplication as reasonably required to carry out the research project is permitted; sale of all
    or part of the data on any media is not. There are no fees associated with these restrictions.
  data_use_permission: general_research_use

ip_restrictions:
  restrictions:
  - >-
      The data may be protected by copyright and other rights, including other intellectual property
      rights; nothing in the agreement transfers any intellectual property rights in or relating to
      the data to the recipient.
  - >-
      Recipients agree not to make intellectual property claims on the data and not to use
      intellectual property protection in ways that would prevent or block access to, or use of, any
      element of the data or conclusions drawn directly from it.
  - >-
      Recipients who perform further research adding intellectual and resource capital may obtain
      intellectual property rights on downstream discoveries, but agree to implement licensing
      policies that will not obstruct further research and to respect the Fort Lauderdale Agreement.
  - >-
      No intellectual-property-based restrictions have been imposed by third parties on the data
      associated with the instances.

regulatory_restrictions:
  regulatory_restrictions:
  - >-
    No export controls apply to the dataset.
  confidentiality_level: restricted
  hipaa_compliant: compliant
  other_compliance: >-
    HIPAA de-identification rules were applied and direct identifiers removed. The data transferred
    under the Data Transfer and Use Agreement is covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality.
    Recipients must store the data with administrative, physical and technical safeguards adequate to
    protect personally identifiable information, must restrict access to authorized persons, and must
    report any unauthorized use or disclosure to the provider within five business days of discovery.
  source_caveats: >-
    The Data Transfer and Use Agreement characterizes the transferred data as personally identifiable
    information under OMB Memorandum M-07-16 and states that it is "not covered under HIPAA, FERPA,
    or similar laws", while the dataset documentation records that HIPAA de-identification rules were
    applied to the released dataset; both statements are recorded rather than reconciled.

data_governance:
  committee_name: Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)
  accountable_organization:
    name: University of South Florida Board of Trustees
    description: >-
      Named as the Provider Institution in the Data Transfer and Use Agreement for the Bridge2AI
      Voice as a Biomarker of Health project.
  access_review_process: >-
    Access to the feature-only release is granted through registered access: users register on
    PhysioNet, confirm their identity under the Registered Access License, and sign the Bridge2AI
    Voice Registered Access Agreement; from version 3.0.0 the applicant must be a credentialed
    PhysioNet user. Access to the raw audio is granted through controlled access: the applicant
    completes a Data Access Request Form and a Data Use Agreement, submits the application to the
    Data Access Compliance Office for review, and on approval has a Data Use and Transfer Agreement
    signed by an authorized official at their institution. The agreement takes effect only upon
    review and approval by the Data Access Compliance Office, which requires a distinct application.
    Requests for raw audio are directed to the access committee at DACO@b2ai-voice.org and the audio
    is served through Synapse.
  stewardship_roles:
  - Provider Institution, which supplies the data and may terminate the agreement
  - Provider Scientist, who signs alongside the Provider Institutional Official
  - >-
      Recipient Institution and Recipient Authorized Institutional Official, who bind the institution
      and warrant compliance
  - >-
      Recipient Scientist, who must retain control over the data and restrict its use to Authorized
      Persons named in the agreement
  - Data Access Compliance Office, which reviews and approves each controlled access application
  notes: >-
    The sources name an office rather than a named individual as the access contact; requests are
    directed to the Data Access Compliance Office mailbox, DACO@b2ai-voice.org. The project
    documentation additionally publishes a memorandum setting out the ethical justification for
    controlled access to raw voice data samples, explaining the reasoning behind this governance
    structure, and records that the fields treated as sensitive and removed from the release were
    identified by a team of ethicists.

third_party_sharing:
- is_shared: true
  notes: >-
    The dataset is distributed broadly to individuals outside the entity that created it, through a
    data publishing platform that provides publicly accessible metadata and a DOI while the dataset
    itself requires registered or credentialed access. Collaborators at other research organizations,
    and other research teams at the same organization, must apply independently for access to the raw
    data and sign their own Data Transfer and Use Agreement.

distribution_formats:
- format: TSV
  media_type: text/tab-separated-values
  description: >-
    Tab-delimited tables: the phenotype tables (confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment,
    questionnaire and task), the per-recording static features, and the audio quality metrics.
  access_urls:
  - https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/
- format: JSON
  media_type: application/json
  description: >-
    JSON data dictionaries accompanying each data file and sharing its file stem, giving a
    description of each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data
    type of the response.
  access_urls:
  - https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/
- format: Parquet
  description: >-
    Apache Parquet, an open-source column-oriented data file format, used for the dense binary
    features: phonetic posteriorgrams, the four sparc feature files, the four torchaudio feature
    files and the per-recording metadata file. Each element carries participant_id, session_id,
    task_name, n_frames and the feature tensor.
  access_urls:
  - https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/
  notes: >-
    No IANA media type for Parquet is stated by the sources, so none is recorded.

distribution_dates:
- release_dates:
  - "Version 1.1: 17 January 2025"
  - "Version 2.0.0: 16 April 2025"
  - "Version 2.0.1: 18 August 2025"
  - "Version 3.0.0: 16 December 2025"
  - "Version 3.1.0: 1 May 2026"
  notes: >-
    Version 1.0 was published earlier on the Health Data Nexus platform; the documentation records
    that the data was published and made available at the end of November 2024.

existing_uses:
- examples:
  - >-
      A restricted version of the dataset containing raw audio has been used in the Bridge2AI Summer
      School and hackathon.

future_use_impacts:
- impact_details: >-
    The dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors, so users
    should consider the multivariate distribution when assessing utility for different questions;
    unexamined use could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups.
- impact_details: >-
    Use outside research — in hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments or surveillance —
    could produce discrimination or harm on the basis of health conditions or voice characteristics,
    which is why such applications are excluded by the access agreement.

external_resources:
- external_resources:
  - >-
    b2aiprep, the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset, to process the raw audio into
    the released features and to merge the source data into the phenotype files, at
    https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep; version 3.0.0 generated this release. SenseLab, used for
    processing audio files for research tasks, at https://github.com/sensein/senselab.
  restrictions:
  - Apache-2.0 license
- external_resources:
  - >-
    The Bridge2AI REDCap data dictionary, metadata and instrument PDFs, at
    https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap and archived on Zenodo at
    https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724.
  restrictions:
  - MIT license
- external_resources:
  - >-
    The source code for the project documentation and dashboards at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/,
    held at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs and archived on Zenodo at
    https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653.
  restrictions:
  - MIT license
- external_resources:
  - >-
    Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, published by the project as supporting
    material.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    The protocol development publication: Bensoussan, Yael, et al. "Developing Multi-Disorder Voice
    Protocols: A team science approach involving clinical expertise, bioethics, standards, and DEI."
    Proc. Interspeech 2024, 1445-1449, https://www.isca-archive.org/interspeech_2024/bensoussan24_interspeech.html
  source_caveats: >-
    The project documentation's healthsheet answers that the dataset "is self-contained" and gives no
    guarantees regarding external resources; the resources listed here are the supporting code,
    metadata and publications the same documentation points to.

  target_dataset: "syn72370534"

  target_dataset: "10.13026/h995-bt35"

  target_dataset: "10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926"
  notes: >-
    The publication describing development of the multi-disorder voice protocols used for collection.

file_collections:
- id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#features
  name: features
  path: features
  collection_type: processed_data
  description: >-
    Audio-derived features for each recording. Dense features are distributed as Apache Parquet
    files, each element carrying participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames and the feature
    tensor; per-recording scalar features and audio quality metrics are distributed as tab-delimited
    files. Every data file is accompanied by a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem and
    describing the feature and the processing used to prepare it.
  resources:
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-torchaudio-spectrogram
    name: torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Spectrograms of dimension 201 by T generated with a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a
      400-point FFT; 29,278 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-torchaudio-mel-spectrogram
    name: torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Mel spectrograms of dimension 60 by T generated with a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length, a
      400-point FFT and 60 Mel bins; 29,278 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-torchaudio-mfcc
    name: torchaudio_mfcc.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Mel-frequency cepstrum coefficients of dimension 60 by T using the same parameters as the Mel
      spectrograms; 29,278 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-torchaudio-pitch
    name: torchaudio_pitch.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Detected pitch (fundamental frequency) over time, dimension T, with minimum and maximum pitch
      of 80 and 500; 32,522 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-sparc-ema
    name: sparc_ema.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Estimated electromagnetic articulography from a deep learning model, dimension T by 12, the
      twelve values being X and Y positions of tongue dorsum, tongue body, tongue tip, lower incisor,
      upper lip and lower lip; 28,640 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-sparc-loudness
    name: sparc_loudness.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Estimated loudness based on the average absolute amplitude of the waveform, dimension T, using
      20 ms windows; 31,855 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-sparc-periodicity
    name: sparc_periodicity.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Estimated periodicity, the confidence of pitch presence, derived using 20 ms windows, dimension
      T; 31,872 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-sparc-pitch
    name: sparc_pitch.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Estimated fundamental frequency of the audio signal over a range of 50 to 550 Hz, dimension T,
      computed with a different algorithm from the torchaudio pitch; 31,872 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-ppgs
    name: ppgs.parquet
    file_type: data_file
    description: >-
      Phonetic posteriorgram probabilities across 40 phoneme categories, dimension 40 by T, at a
      frame rate of 100 Hz; 29,289 records.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-static-features
    name: static_features.tsv
    file_type: data_file
    format: TSV
    media_type: text/tab-separated-values
    description: >-
      Features derived from the raw audio with one feature per audio recording, drawn from openSMILE,
      Praat, parselmouth and torchaudio; one row per unique recording.
  - id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#file-audio-quality-metrics
    name: audio_quality_metrics.tsv
    file_type: data_file
    format: TSV
    media_type: text/tab-separated-values
    description: >-
      One feature per audio recording derived from the raw audio, relating to quality control metrics.
- id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#phenotype
  name: phenotype
  path: phenotype
  collection_type: other
  description: >-
    Organized information collected from the participant or another individual during their
    encounter, as tab-delimited files each paired with a JSON data dictionary, grouped into
    confounders, demographics, diagnosis (per-condition files covering airway stenosis, amyotrophic
    lateral sclerosis, anxiety, benign lesions, bipolar disorder, cognitive impairment, control,
    COPD and asthma, depression, glottic insufficiency, laryngeal cancer, laryngeal dystonia,
    laryngitis, muscle tension dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, precancerous lesions, unexplained
    chronic cough and unilateral vocal fold paralysis), enrollment (eligibility, enrollment form,
    participant), questionnaire (ADHD adult, custom affect scale, DSM-5 adult, dyspnea index, GAD-7,
    Leicester cough questionnaire, PANAS, PHQ-9, productive vocabulary, psychiatric history, PTSD
    adult, VHI-10, voice perception) and task (acoustic task, harvard sentences, random item
    generation, recording, session, stroop, winograd).
- id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#metadata
  name: metadata
  path: metadata
  collection_type: metadata
  description: >-
    A binary Parquet file and its data dictionary holding per-recording metadata, including task
    instructions and prompts and information about the microphone used and its gain.

maintainers:
- role: academic_institution
  maintainer_details: >-
    PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, hosts the release and
    provides continued access to credentialed researchers.
- role: government_agency
  maintainer_details: >-
    The dataset is supported by the NIH via the Bridge2AI project, under NIH Common Fund award

- role: researcher
  maintainer_details: >-

updates:
  update_details: >-
    The project documentation states that further versions of the dataset will be released on a
    semi-annual (twice a year) basis, distributed as new versions of the dataset, with users notified
    through news items on the hosting platform and through standard communication channels; that
    statement is a plan written against the Health Data Nexus platform and an earlier release, not an
    observed cadence. Published versions to date are 1.0 on Health Data Nexus, then 1.1 (17 January
    2025), 2.0.0 (16 April 2025), 2.0.1 (18 August 2025), 3.0.0 (16 December 2025) and 3.1.0 (1 May
    2026).

version_access:
  latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42
  versions_available:
  - "1.1 — 17 January 2025 — doi:10.13026/249v-w155"
  - "2.0.0 — 16 April 2025"
  - "2.0.1 — 18 August 2025"
  - "3.0.0 — 16 December 2025 — doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68"
  - "3.1.0 — 1 May 2026 — doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66"
  version_details: >-
    Each version of the dataset has a unique DOI, and by default older versions continue to be
    supported, hosted and made available to researchers, though the dataset publishers reserve the
    right to remove access to older versions. The files for version 1.1 are no longer available from
    PhysioNet. Version 1.0 was published on the Health Data Nexus platform under
    doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84.

errata:
- erratum_details: >-
    Version 2.0 reprocessed the spectrograms to fix minor issues identified in the previous release
    and removed all spectrograms and Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients derived from free-speech
    files. Version 2.0.1 corrected the authorship list. Version 3.1.0 fixed broken parquet files
    carried over from the previous release, updated validated diagnosis information across
    conditions with back-filled information, rearranged some phenotypic files and renamed certain
    gold standard variable names.
  source_caveats: >-
    The project documentation states that there is no erratum and that a changelog for each dataset
    version is published online with the dataset metadata; the corrections recorded here are taken
    from those per-version release notes.

retention_limit:
  retention_period: Indefinite for the published dataset; two years or less for recipients of the raw data
  retention_details: >-
    Once data is contributed, the data will be retained as long as it is useful for research
    purposes, possibly indefinitely. Recipients of the raw voice data under the Data Transfer and Use
    Agreement hold it for a shorter term: two years after the start date, upon completion of the
    project, upon termination, or upon expiration of the applicable ethics approval, whichever occurs
    first, after which the data is destroyed in accordance with the provider's instructions and a
    written certification of destruction is submitted within thirty days. Identifiable data and the
    sheets linking participant numbers to participant information are held by each collecting
    institution for a maximum of ten years after study completion and then destroyed.

extension_mechanism:
  contribution_url: https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep
  extension_details: >-
    Others may publish a derivative dataset that references the original source, made available under
    the same conditions as the source data. For the code used to produce the data, the open-source
    repositories provide discussion forums and issue pages for public discussion of data
    preprocessing, and a pull request mechanism for contributing improvements to the preprocessing
    code.

The Reproducibility section is present in my instructions, and its sentence reads, verbatim:

> Repeatability must be measured on unchanged records under the same evaluator model and definition, because even a fixed or zero sampling temperature does not guarantee identical semantic judgements.

This is consistent with the current instrument (it conditions repeatability on both evaluator model *and* definition, and disclaims determinism even at fixed/zero temperature), so I proceeded. `instrument_sha256` recorded as `9d08b5f3…0e7dd3`.

**VOICE / claudecode_api — 78/88 = 88.6%** (fixed and normalized coincide; `excluded_max_points: 0`, `adjusted_max_points: 88`, `questions_not_applicable: 0`).

All four conditional triggers resolved as **met**, each on fields belonging to a different question per the anti-circular rule:
- **Human subjects** (Q8, Q15) — `description`'s "833 adult participants", `keywords`, `collection_mechanisms`.
- **Datasets shared** (Q10, Q17) — `page`, `access_urls` on every format, reuse-permitting licence.
- **Software output** (Q11) — `external_resources` names four GitHub repositories; `extension_mechanism.contribution_url` independently.
- **Collection + shared** (Q12, Q13) — collection fields populated plus the sharing limb.

Category scores: Structural 18/21, Metadata 19/21, Technical 22/25, FAIRness 19/21.

Scores below maximum, with reasons: Q3 keywords 3 (only four generic terms); Q4 formats 4 (exactly three formats, lifted by exceptional per-file enumeration); Q8 ethics 4 (record states no DPIA was conducted); Q10 interop 4 (no data-level standard asserted); Q11 tools 4 (versions pinned only for b2aiprep); Q13 versioning 4; Q15 human subjects 4 (no demographic figures); Q18 4 (social-impact half thin); Q20 4 (no AIO mappings, qualitative fairness only).

Two consistency checks failed. The load-bearing one: `version_access.latest_version_doi` is `doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42`, which matches no entry in the record's own `versions_available`, is not the top-level DOI, and is not the 3.0.0 or pediatric DOI — a pointing error in exactly the field used to locate the current release. The second is the disclosed HIPAA tension (`hipaa_compliant: compliant` against the quoted DTUA text "not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws"); because the record flags it rather than concealing it, I logged it as a content-accuracy issue rather than deducting twice for it.

Worth noting as a distinguishing feature of this record: it discloses negative findings against interest (no DPIA, k-anonymity not achieved, transcription models unaudited, v1.1 files unretrievable, BIDS conformance deliberately *not* carried over from a differing layout). That candour raised confidence in the claims I could not otherwise verify, and I said so in the insights rather than rewarding it with score inflation.
